blocks.text: Hex-1-ene and cyclohexane have the same molecular formula, C6H12, but different structures: they are isomers. Both have two hydrogen atoms fewer than the saturated alkane hexane, C6H14: they are deficient by two hydrogen atoms. This deficiency corresponds to the degree of unsaturation of the compound. A compound has one degree of unsaturation for every two hydrogen atoms that are missing, so both have an IHD of 1.

blocks.title: Index of hydrogen deficiency (IHD)
blocks.text: The degree of unsaturation (U), or index of hydrogen deficiency (IHD), is the difference in the number of pairs of hydrogen atoms between the compound and the acyclic alkane with the same number of carbon atoms. Each double bond or ring removes two hydrogen atoms and counts as one; a triple bond counts as two.

For example, C4H6 has four hydrogen atoms fewer than the saturated C4H10, so it has two degrees of unsaturation (IHD = 2). For a hydrocarbon, IHD = (2 x number of carbons + 2 - number of hydrogens) / 2.

Knowing the IHD gives clues to the structure, and it can be found just by looking at the formula. If the IHD is 0, the compound has no rings and no double bonds. If it is 1, the compound has either one ring or one double bond, but not both. If it is 2, it could have two rings, two double bonds, one of each, or one triple bond. The IHD also helps in choosing which analytical technique would be best for the compound.

blocks.alt: Top: the skeletal formulas of hex-1-ene (a chain with one C=C at the end) and cyclohexane (a six-membered ring), both C6H12 and two H atoms short of hexane, each with IHD 1; notes say a C=C or a ring counts 1 and a triple bond 2. Bottom: the book's table, CnH2n+2 IHD 0 (open-chain alkane only), CnH2n IHD 1 (one double bond or one ring), CnH2n-2 IHD 2 (two double bonds, two rings, one of each, or one triple bond), and IHD = (2 x carbons + 2 - hydrogens) / 2.

blocks.long_description: Compare the formula with the saturated alkane that has the same number of carbons: every two missing hydrogens means one ring or one double bond. The formula alone tells how many, but not which.

items: Calculate the IHD of (i) C6H6, (ii) C6H12, (iii) C4H4, and suggest a structure for each.
A hopane has the formula C30H62. Find its IHD and say whether it is saturated.
